subtype: A friend noticing a too-fast bond [Observer]
passage:
"You skipped cricket nets again," Aadhya said, sliding her tray beside her old friend Madhav in the hostel mess.
"Nisha wanted to video call. She gets upset if I'm not free."
"And Friday's movie? And the lab group?"
"I'll catch up. Aadhya, you don't get it. It's been one week and it feels like we've known each other forever."
Aadhya stirred her dal. "I'm happy you're happy. Can I say one thing, and you can ignore it?"
"Go on."
"In one week you've dropped nets, the movie and me. Every sentence starts with Nisha. That's a lot of speed."
Madhav's jaw tightened. "So you think I'm stupid."
"No. I think you're excited, and that's allowed. I just miss you, and I'd like to meet Nisha too."
He looked at his phone, then at her. "She said my friends would be jealous."
"Maybe some are. I'm not going anywhere. Sunday breakfast, same table, whenever you want."

qa.q: What did Madhav skip, according to Aadhya?
qa.a: Madhav skipped cricket nets again, and Aadhya also mentioned Friday's movie and the lab group.

qa.q: What is Aadhya feeling as she talks to Madhav?
qa.a: Aadhya is glad Madhav is happy but worried by the speed, and she misses him, as she says, "I just miss you."

qa.q: Which choice of Aadhya's kept the door open for Madhav?
qa.a: Aadhya named what she saw without insulting Nisha, said she missed him, and offered Sunday breakfast at the same table, so he can come back without shame.

qa.q: How might Madhav later see the offer of a standing Sunday breakfast?
qa.a: If things with Nisha grow tense, he may remember that Aadhya did not scold him and feel safe returning to that table.

grounding: A young woman notices a friend drop his usual plans a week into a new relationship, names the speed kindly, and stays available without shaming him.

subtype: A friend noticing a too-fast bond [Observer]
passage:
Last March my roommate Ojas met someone at a dance workshop, and by the next Saturday I barely recognised our flat. Our Sunday grocery run? Cancelled. The group trip to the waterfall? Ojas stayed back to wait for a call. Every dinner story was about Kiran: Kiran's poems, Kiran saying they were soulmates, Kiran wanting Ojas to move in by summer.
I'm Reena, and I'm bad at hard talks. I wrote three versions of what to say and deleted them all. In the end I just said, over chai, "I've noticed you've stopped doing the things that were yours. I might be wrong. I'm not going to lecture. I just miss you."
Ojas went quiet, then said I didn't understand real love. I said maybe not, and that the Sunday grocery run would still happen at ten.
Three Sundays later, Ojas showed up at ten, eyes puffy, holding the cloth bags.

qa.a: Ojas met Kiran at a dance workshop.

qa.q: Why did Reena delete three versions of what to say?
qa.a: Reena was nervous about hurting Ojas or sounding like a lecture, and admits to being bad at hard talks.

qa.q: Why was Reena's reply to "you don't understand real love" a wise choice?
qa.a: Reena did not argue or try to win; keeping the Sunday grocery run open at ten gave Ojas a way back without losing face.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Ojas to show up at ten, three Sundays later?
qa.a: Ojas likely felt hurt and embarrassed, but also relieved that the old plan was still there and that no one would say "I told you so".

grounding: A roommate sees Ojas give up shared routines within a week of meeting someone, gently names it once, and keeps a standing plan open without shaming.
